ayahs.1: By the dawn—Allah swears by the break of morning, when darkness lifts and a new day begins, as witness to truths that only attentive hearts grasp.
ayahs.2: And the ten nights—the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, among the most sacred times for worship, sacrifice, and drawing near to Allah.
ayahs.3: And the even and the odd—paired rhythms in creation and time, signs that nothing in the universe is random chaos.
ayahs.4: And the night when it passes—when darkness thins and retreats, reminding you that no state lasts unchanged forever.
ayahs.5: Is this oath not enough for those who reflect—who see that Allah's appointed times of worship carry real weight?
ayahs.6: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad—
ayahs.7: The people of Iram, possessed of towering stature,
ayahs.8: The likes of whom were never built in any land?
ayahs.9: And Thamud, who carved their homes into the rocks of the valley?
ayahs.10: And Pharaoh, master of fortified pillars?
ayahs.11: They all transgressed across their lands,
ayahs.12: Spreading much corruption there—oppression, arrogance, and harm to the vulnerable.
ayahs.13: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.
ayahs.14: Your Lord is truly Ever-Watchful—not unaware when the powerful abuse the weak.
ayahs.15: Whenever a human being is tested by their Lord with generosity and ease, they boast, "My Lord has honoured me!"—mistaking wealth for divine approval.
ayahs.16: But when He tests them by restricting provision, they protest, "My Lord has humiliated me!"—mistaking hardship for divine rejection.
ayahs.17: No! You do not honour the orphan—
ayahs.18: Nor urge one another to feed the poor—
ayahs.19: And you devour inheritance greedily, by trickery or outright theft—
ayahs.20: And you love wealth with consuming passion, as if accumulation were the purpose of life.
ayahs.21: Enough! When the earth is crushed, ground repeatedly to dust—
ayahs.22: And your Lord comes—with angels ranked in rows, an image of the Day when hidden realities become visible—
ayahs.23: And Hell is brought near that Day—then every soul remembers, but remembrance then cannot buy back a life misspent.
ayahs.24: They will cry, "If only I had sent ahead something for my real life!"—the Akhirah, the everlasting life that mattered all along.
ayahs.25: On that Day no one will punish as He punishes—
ayahs.26: And no one will bind as He binds.
ayahs.27: O tranquil soul—the nafs mutma'innah, the soul at peace with Allah, no longer torn between craving and fear—
ayahs.28: Return to your Rabb, pleased and well pleasing—satisfied with His decree and accepted by Him.
